decisions.choice: the tent of meeting: the tent where God met with Moses and with Israel
decisions.reason: This is the tent Moses set up in Exodus 40, also called the dwelling place (the tabernacle). "Meeting" comes from a verb for meeting at a set time or place: God said, "There I will meet with you" (Exodus 25:22; 29:42-43). It is the place from which God speaks and where offerings are brought, at its entrance (verse 3).

decisions.choice: he called to Moses: Yahweh speaks from the tent that his glory has just filled
decisions.reason: Exodus ends with the glory of Yahweh filling the tent, so that Moses could not go in (Exodus 40:34-35). Leviticus begins with God calling to Moses from inside it. The first verb has no subject, which is supplied by "Yahweh" in the next clause. The book's Hebrew name is its first word, "And he called".

decisions.choice: the meeting tent
decisions.reason: Readable says "the meeting tent", which a young reader can follow more easily than "tent of meeting". Literal and Balanced keep "the tent of meeting".

decisions.choice: He said
decisions.reason: "Saying" introduces God's words. Balanced and Readable turn it into "He said" and put "from the tent" where it reads naturally.

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR" (default); "Yahvé" with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Genesis and Exodus: the name YHWH is written "el SEÑOR" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD"; the divine name setting gives "Yahvé", the usual Spanish form of the name. The span takes in the article and its contraction ("del SEÑOR|de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR|a Yahvé"). Adonai YHWH, where it occurs, is "Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}". "Jehová", the form of the Reina-Valera tradition, is the alternative a reviewer may prefer.

decisions.choice: no deity pronoun span on "llamó"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Genesis and Exodus: the deity pronoun setting goes on the Spanish words for God that Spanish writes out (él, lo, le, su, mí, me, mi, tú, te, ti, tu), lowercase by default and capitalised as the alternative. Here the subject of "llamó" is only in the verb, as in the Hebrew, so Spanish has no span where the English "he" has one.

decisions.choice: "la Tienda del Encuentro" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Exodus: "Encuentro" says plainly that this is where God meets with Moses and Israel (m1), and is clear enough for Readable too, where the English says "the meeting tent". "Tabernáculo" is kept for the dwelling (mishkan).

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" (default); "Yahvé" with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Genesis and Exodus: the name YHWH is written "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD" and the Spanish "el SEÑOR"; the divine name setting gives "Yahvé", the usual French form of the name. The span takes in the article and its contraction ("du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé", "au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé"). Adonai YHWH, where it occurs, is "le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}". "L'Éternel", used in French Protestant Bibles since the Reformation, is the alternative a native reviewer may prefer; it was not made the default because it interprets the name rather than giving either the name or the traditional title "Lord".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Genesis and Exodus: every pronoun for God takes the deity pronoun setting, lowercase by default and capitalised as the alternative (il, lui, le, l', son, sa, ses, and moi, me, m', mon, ma, mes, toi, te, tu, ton when God speaks or is spoken to, including an inverted "-tu"). "Je" has no span, and a pronoun opening a sentence is written plainly with its capital (Balanced and Readable "Il dit", "Il lui a dit").

decisions.choice: "la tente de la Rencontre" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Exodus: "la Rencontre" says plainly that this is where God meets with Moses and Israel (m1), and serves Readable as well, where the English says "the meeting tent". "Assignation" is now a legal word to most readers.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("appela", "parla", "dit"); passé composé at Readable ("a appelé", "a dit")
decisions.reason: As docs/french-style.md section 3, for the narrative verses of Leviticus. The laws that follow are in the forms French uses for commands (see the next verse).

decisions.choice: "BWANA" (default); "Yahwe" with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Genesis and Exodus: the name YHWH is written "BWANA" (Lord) in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD"; the divine name setting gives "Yahwe", the name in Swahili spelling. Adonai YHWH, where it occurs, is "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}". "Yehova" is the older form some Swahili readers know; a reviewer may prefer it as the alternative.

decisions.choice: no deity pronoun span: "Akamwita Musa"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Genesis and Exodus: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb, where no capital is possible, so the deity pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns for God (yeye, naye, mimi, nami, wewe, and the possessives wake, yake, wangu, yako...), even where the English has none. Here the subject is only in the verb, so there is no span. In Leviticus God speaks in the first person ("mimi ni BWANA"), and those free pronouns take the span.

decisions.choice: "Hema la Kukutania" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Exodus: "kukutania" says that this is the tent where God meets with Moses and Israel (m1), not a hall for meetings, as "mkutano" would suggest. "Hema" takes class 5 agreement ("la"), as in standard Swahili.

decisions.choice: "Lều Hội Kiến" at every level; "phán" for God speaking
alternatives: "lều gặp gỡ" at Readable, as the English Readable says "the meeting tent"
decisions.reason: The term the Pentateuch sheet settles for the tent of meeting, already used in Joshua; it is kept at Readable too so the one tent has one name through Leviticus. "phán" is the verb kept for God speaking (Vietnamese style guide). Recorded once for Leviticus 1-9.

decisions.choice: "회막" for the tent of meeting at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: The term sheet for Exodus to Deuteronomy settles "회막"; the English Readable's "meeting tent" is a plainer English phrase, but Korean readers know "회막" as the name of this tent, so one word is kept through the book.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span: "그분께서" with the honorific
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting the English marks on "He" has nothing to change; respect for God is carried by "그분", "께서" and the honorific "-시-" at every level, as the Korean style guide sets for the whole Bible.

decisions.choice: a tenda do encontro
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Exodus (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md): "a tenda do encontro" names the tent where God meets with Moses and Israel (m1). It is already plain Portuguese, so Readable keeps it where the English Readable changes to "the meeting tent". "Tenda da congregação", the older name, makes it a place where the people gather.

decisions.choice: offering: something brought near to God
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "bring near", and the verse uses both: "when anyone brings near an offering ... you shall bring near your offering". It is the general word for whatever is presented to God: animals (chapters 1 and 3), grain (2:1) and gifts for the sanctuary (Numbers 7:3). By it a worshiper comes near to God.

decisions.choice: anyone: any human being, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being, not the word for a male. The laws that follow are for whoever brings an offering; a woman also brings a burnt offering after childbirth (12:6).

decisions.choice: the livestock, the herd, the flock: domestic animals only
decisions.reason: "Livestock" is then narrowed to the herd (cattle, verse 3) and the flock (sheep and goats, verse 10). Wild animals are not offered. Birds, allowed in verse 14, are the one exception.

decisions.choice: brings / bring
decisions.reason: "Bring near" is kept at Literal to show the link between the verb and the noun "offering". Balanced and Readable say "bring" or "present". Readable lists the animals of the herd and flock: cattle, sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: anyone / one of you / you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is already inclusive, so no gender setting is needed. In the laws that follow the Hebrew says "he" for this person; Literal keeps "he", Balanced uses "the worshiper", "they" or a passive, and Readable speaks to the reader as "you", as this verse already does.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" (L); "los israelitas" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Exodus: the phrase means the whole people, women as well as men. Spanish "hijos" already includes daughters, so Literal keeps "los hijos de Israel" and Balanced and Readable say "los israelitas", both without the gender setting the English needs.

decisions.choice: ustedes forms by default (ustedes, presentarán, su, traigan); vosotros forms with the plural-you setting (vosotros, presentaréis, vuestra, traigáis)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Genesis and Exodus: whenever several people are addressed, Spanish must choose a plural form of address. The default is the "ustedes" form used by most Spanish speakers; the plural-you setting gives the "vosotros" form of Spain. The span covers each verb, pronoun or possessive that changes. Where a law speaks of one worshiper, Literal and Balanced use the third person, and Readable addresses that person as "tú" (verse 3), with no span.

decisions.choice: future for the laws at Literal and Balanced ("presentarán", "será"); "tiene que", "debe" or the imperative at Readable ("tiene que ser", "Llévalo")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: the laws are given in the forms Spanish uses for commands. Literal and Balanced keep the future of legal style, as the Hebrew uses its future-like form; Readable uses "tener que", "deber" or a plain imperative, as the English Readable uses "must".

decisions.choice: les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël (L); les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Exodus: the phrase means the whole people, women as well as men, so the default is inclusive, as in English: "les enfants d'Israël" at Literal, which keeps the family word, and "les Israélites" at Balanced and Readable. The setting gives the traditional "fils d'Israël".

decisions.choice: future for the laws at Literal and Balanced ("vous ferez approcher", "il le prendra", "il amènera"); "tu dois", "il doit" or the imperative at Readable ("il doit être pris", "Amène-le")
alternatives: the present of legal style at Balanced
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: the laws are given in the forms French uses for commands. Literal and Balanced use the future, the classic form of French legal and biblical commands; Readable uses "devoir" or a plain imperative, as the English Readable uses "must".

decisions.choice: "wana wa Israeli" (L); "Waisraeli" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus, as in Exodus: the phrase means the whole people, women as well as men. Swahili "wana" already includes daughters, so no setting is needed; Balanced and Readable say "Waisraeli", the plain name of the people.

decisions.choice: -ta- future or the subjunctive for the laws at Literal and Balanced ("mtasogeza", "atatoka", "atamleta"); "lazima" or plain commands at Readable ("lazima awe", "Mlete")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: the laws are given in the forms Swahili uses for commands. Literal and Balanced use the -ta- future or the subjunctive; Readable says "lazima" or gives a plain command, as the English Readable uses "must".

decisions.choice: "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (Literal); "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (Balanced, Readable), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English, such as "con trai Y-sơ-ra-ên"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch sheet's forms. "con cháu" and "dân" already include men and women, so Vietnamese has no second wording for the gender setting. Book-wide for Leviticus 1-9.

decisions.choice: God's law addresses the people as "các ngươi" / "ngươi" at Literal and Balanced; Readable speaks of the worshiper in the third person ("ai", "người ấy", "người dâng") where the English Readable says "you"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch sheet uses "ngươi" / "các ngươi" for God's commands and "người ấy" for an offerer in the third person. Vietnamese has no neutral "you"; a plain third person keeps Readable simple without the stern "ngươi". The meaning, a rule for any worshiper, is the same. Book-wide for Leviticus 1-9.

decisions.choice: "dâng" for "bring near"; "lễ vật" for the offering (qorban)
decisions.reason: "dâng" is the ordinary Vietnamese verb for presenting something to God and keeps the sense of bringing it near; "lễ vật" is the general word for a gift to God, leaving "của lễ ..." and "tế lễ ..." for the named offerings.

decisions.choice: God's commands in the plain written style: "-하라" / "-해야 한다" at Literal and Balanced, "-해야 한다" / "-하면 안 된다" at Readable; the offerer and the priest in the third person take the plain style ("-해야 한다")
decisions.reason: The Exodus-Deuteronomy term sheet sets this for all the laws, so that Leviticus reads as one voice; God speaks to Moses in 해라체 as in Genesis, and the laws he gives are written in the plain style of a code.

decisions.choice: "가까이 바치다" for the verb "bring near" at Literal; "바치다" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb for offering is "bring near"; Literal keeps the picture with "가까이", while the other levels use the ordinary word for presenting an offering. "제물" renders the general word "offering" at every level.

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L); os israelitas (B, R); no gender setting
alternatives: os filhos e as filhas de Israel, under a gender setting
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as Exodus 1:7 and docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md set it: the English needs a gender setting because "sons" names only men, but Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters and "os israelitas" names the whole people, so there is nothing for a setting to change.

decisions.choice: alguém; oferecer ... uma oferta (L)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the Hebrew word is the general word for a human being (m2), and Portuguese "alguém" already means anyone, so it takes no gender setting, and the "ele" that refers back to it in the laws is ordinary generic Portuguese. Literal says "oferecer ... oferta" because the Portuguese verb and noun share a root, as the Hebrew "bring near" and "offering" do (m1); "fazer chegar perto" would keep the picture but not the link.

records.literal_gloss: If [a] burnt offering [is] his offering from the herd, [a] male unblemished he will bring near it; to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting he will bring near it, for his acceptance before Yahweh.

en.L: If his offering [is] a burnt offering from the herd, he shall bring near a male, unblemished; to the entrance of the tent of meeting he shall bring it near, for his acceptance before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: A burnt offering from the herd must be a male without defect. It is to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will accept the one who offers it.
en.R: If you bring a burnt offering from your cattle, it must be a male with nothing wrong with it. Bring it to the entrance of the meeting tent. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will accept you.

es.L: Si su ofrenda [es] holocausto de la vacada, presentará un macho sin defecto; a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro lo presentará, para ser aceptado delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: El holocausto de ganado vacuno será un macho sin defecto. Se llevará a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro, para que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acepte a quien lo ofrece.
es.R: Si traes un holocausto de tus vacas, tiene que ser un macho que no tenga nada malo. Llévalo a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro. Así {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te aceptará.

fr.L: Si son offrande [est] un holocauste de gros bétail, il fera approcher un mâle sans défaut ; il le fera approcher à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre, afin d’être agréé devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: L’holocauste pris dans le gros bétail sera un mâle sans défaut. On l’amènera à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre, afin que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} accueille favorablement celui qui l’offre.
fr.R: Si tu offres un holocauste pris parmi tes bœufs, ce doit être un mâle qui n’a rien d’abîmé. Amène-le à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre. Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’acceptera.

sw.L: Ikiwa sadaka yake [ni] sadaka ya kuteketezwa kutoka kwa ng'ombe, atasogeza dume asiye na kasoro; atamsogeza kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania, ili akubaliwe mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Sadaka ya kuteketezwa kutoka kwa kundi la ng'ombe itakuwa dume asiye na kasoro. Ataletwa kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania, ili {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amkubali yule anayemtoa.
sw.R: Ukileta sadaka ya kuteketezwa kutoka kwa ng'ombe wako, lazima awe dume asiye na tatizo lolote. Mlete kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania. Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakukubali.

ko.L: 만일 그의 제물이 소 떼에서 [바치는] 번제물이면, 그는 흠 없는 수컷을 가까이 바쳐야 한다. 그는 그것을 회막 입구로 가까이 바쳐서, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 자기가 받아들여지게 해야 한다.
ko.B: 소 떼에서 번제물을 바칠 때에는 흠 없는 수컷을 바쳐야 한다. 그것을 회막 입구로 가져와야 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 바치는 사람을 받아 주신다.
ko.R: 소를 번제물로 바치려면 아무 흠이 없는 수컷을 바쳐야 한다. 그것을 회막 입구로 가져가야 한다. 그러면 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 사람을 받아 주실 것이다.

vi.L: Nếu lễ vật của người ấy [là] một của lễ thiêu từ bầy bò, người ấy phải dâng một con đực không tì vết; người ấy phải dâng nó tại cửa Lều Hội Kiến, để người ấy được chấp nhận trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Nếu của lễ thiêu là một con vật trong bầy bò, thì phải là con đực không tì vết. Người ấy phải đem nó đến cửa Lều Hội Kiến, để được {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chấp nhận.
vi.R: Nếu ai dâng một con bò làm của lễ thiêu, thì đó phải là con đực không tì vết. Người ấy phải đem nó đến cửa Lều Hội Kiến. Như vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ chấp nhận người ấy.

pt.L: Se a sua oferta [for] um holocausto do gado, oferecerá um macho sem defeito; à entrada da tenda do encontro o oferecerá, para a sua aceitação diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: Se a oferta for um holocausto do gado, será um macho sem defeito. Ele será trazido à entrada da tenda do encontro, para que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} aceite quem o oferece.
pt.R: Se trouxeres um holocausto do teu gado, ele deve ser um macho sem nenhum defeito. Deves levá-lo até a entrada da tenda do encontro. Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} te aceitará.

decisions.choice: burnt offering: an offering that goes up whole in smoke
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "go up". All of the animal except its skin (7:8) goes up in smoke on the altar (verse 9), and nothing is eaten. It was offered every morning and evening (Exodus 29:38-42), and could be brought by anyone as a gift, a vow or a plea to God.

decisions.choice: unblemished: whole, with no physical defect
decisions.reason: The word means complete or whole. Of an animal it means one with no defect: 22:17-25 lists what makes an animal unfit, such as blindness, injury or deformity. God is to be given what is whole, not what is damaged (Malachi 1:8). The same word describes people who are blameless (Genesis 6:9; 17:1).

decisions.choice: for his acceptance: so that the worshiper is accepted before Yahweh
decisions.reason: "His" most likely refers to the worshiper, as verse 4 says: "it will be accepted for him" (compare 22:19-21). An older reading takes it as "of his own free will", but the word is used in these laws for God's acceptance of the offerer.

decisions.choice: so that the LORD will accept the one who offers it
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "for his acceptance before the LORD" into a clause with the LORD as the subject, and uses passives so that it does not need "he" for a worshiper who may be a man or a woman.

decisions.choice: with nothing wrong with it; you
decisions.reason: Readable explains "unblemished" in common words and speaks to the reader directly, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: "el holocausto" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: "holocausto" is the established Spanish word for the offering burned whole (m1) and is still understood in that sense. "Ofrenda quemada" is kept for the food offering (verse 9).

decisions.choice: "sin defecto" (L, B); "que no tenga nada malo" (R, as the English)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: "sin defecto" says what the word means of an animal, no physical defect (m2); "sin mancha" suggests a stain.

decisions.choice: "l'holocauste" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: "holocauste" is the established French word for the offering burned whole (m1) and, despite its modern historical sense, every French Bible reader knows it in this one.

decisions.choice: Readable speaks to the worshiper as "tu" ("Si tu offres", "Amène-le")
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "you" for the one who brings the offering, French Readable uses "tu": the Hebrew laws speak of one worshiper ("he"), and Readable addresses that person directly, as Spanish "tú" and Swahili "wewe" do.

decisions.choice: "sadaka ya kuteketezwa" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: the burnt offering is wholly consumed by fire (m1); "kuteketezwa" says it is burned up, not merely burned. The food offering (verse 9) is "sadaka ya kuteketezwa kwa moto".

decisions.choice: "asiye na kasoro" (L, B); "asiye na tatizo lolote" (R, as the English)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: "kasoro" is a physical fault or defect (m2), the agreement following the animal ("dume asiye na kasoro", "isiyo na kasoro" for a class 9 noun). Readable speaks to the worshiper as "wewe" ("Ukileta", "Mlete"), as the English Readable says "you".

decisions.choice: "của lễ thiêu" (burnt offering); "không tì vết" (unblemished)
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch sheet's terms, as Genesis 22 already says "của lễ thiêu". "không tì vết" is plain enough to keep at Readable, so the requirement reads the same at every level.

decisions.choice: "번제" ("번제물" for the animal) and "흠 없는"
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps the established Korean names of the offerings so that the five offerings of Leviticus 1-7 are recognisable; "흠 없는" is the plain word for an animal with no defect. Readable adds "아무" for emphasis rather than a new term.

decisions.choice: o holocausto; sem defeito (L, B), sem nenhum defeito (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md sets them: "holocausto" is the Portuguese name for the offering that goes up whole in smoke (m1), at every level, as in Exodus; "oferta queimada" is kept for the food offering of verse 9, a different Hebrew word. "Sem defeito" is the phrase for an animal with nothing wrong with it (m2); Readable strengthens it to "sem nenhum defeito", as the English Readable says it in common words.

decisions.choice: tu (Readable's address to the worshiper)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: where the English Readable speaks to the worshiper as "you", Portuguese Readable uses "tu", "teu", "te", because it is God's law addressed to each Israelite, and the Pentateuch drafts give God's word to Israel in the singular "tu" (Exodus 13:5; 20). "Vocês" would make one person's offering sound like the whole people's; "você" is kept for people speaking to each other. Where the Hebrew itself speaks to the people in the plural (verse 2), every level says "vocês".

source.text: וְסָמַ֣ךְ יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל רֹ֣אשׁ הָעֹלָ֑ה וְנִרְצָ֥ה ל֖וֹ לְכַפֵּ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will lean his hand on [the] head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted for him to make atonement for him.

en.L: And he shall lean his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted for him, to make atonement for him.
en.B: The worshiper is to lay their hand on the head of the burnt offering, which will then be accepted for them and make atonement for them.
en.R: Put your hand on the head of the animal. Then it will be accepted for you, to make atonement for you.

es.L: Y apoyará su mano sobre la cabeza del holocausto, y le será aceptado para hacer expiación por él.
es.B: El oferente pondrá la mano sobre la cabeza del holocausto, el cual será aceptado en su favor para hacer expiación por él.
es.R: Pon tu mano sobre la cabeza del animal. Entonces será aceptado en tu favor, para hacer expiación por ti.

fr.L: Et il appuiera sa main sur la tête de l’holocauste, et il sera agréé en sa faveur, pour faire l’expiation pour lui.
fr.B: Celui qui l’offre posera la main sur la tête de l’holocauste, qui sera alors agréé en sa faveur et fera l’expiation pour lui.
fr.R: Pose ta main sur la tête de l’animal. Alors il sera accepté en ta faveur, pour faire l’expiation pour toi.

sw.L: Naye ataegemeza mkono wake juu ya kichwa cha sadaka ya kuteketezwa, nayo itakubaliwa kwa ajili yake, ili kufanya upatanisho kwa ajili yake.
sw.B: Anayeitoa ataweka mkono wake juu ya kichwa cha sadaka ya kuteketezwa, nayo itakubaliwa kwa ajili yake na kumfanyia upatanisho.
sw.R: Weka mkono wako juu ya kichwa cha mnyama huyo. Ndipo atakubaliwa kwa ajili yako, ili kukufanyia upatanisho.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 번제물의 머리 위에 자기 손을 얹어야 한다. 그러면 그것이 그를 위하여 받아들여져, 그를 위하여 속죄할 것이다.
ko.B: 바치는 사람은 번제물의 머리에 손을 얹어야 한다. 그러면 그 제물이 그를 위하여 받아들여져 그를 위하여 속죄할 것이다.
ko.R: 바치는 사람은 그 짐승의 머리에 손을 얹어야 한다. 그러면 그 짐승이 그 사람을 위하여 받아들여지고, 그 사람을 위하여 속죄가 이루어진다.

vi.L: Và người ấy phải đặt tay mình trên đầu của lễ thiêu, và nó sẽ được chấp nhận cho người ấy, để chuộc tội cho người ấy.
vi.B: Người ấy phải đặt tay trên đầu con vật dâng làm của lễ thiêu, và của lễ ấy sẽ được nhận vì người ấy để chuộc tội cho người ấy.
vi.R: Người dâng phải đặt tay trên đầu con vật. Rồi con vật sẽ được chấp nhận để chuộc tội cho người ấy.

pt.L: E apoiará a mão sobre a cabeça do holocausto, e ele será aceito em seu favor, para fazer expiação por ele.
pt.B: Quem o oferece porá a mão sobre a cabeça do holocausto, e o animal será aceito em seu favor e fará expiação por ele.
pt.R: Deves pôr a mão na cabeça do animal. Então ele será aceito em teu favor, para fazer expiação por ti.

decisions.choice: lean his hand on the head: a gesture marking the animal as the worshiper's own offering
alternatives: a sign that the worshiper's sin passes to the animal
decisions.reason: The verb means to press or lean, not merely to touch. The same act is done for the peace offering (3:2) and the sin offering (4:4). The text does not explain it here. At least it shows that this animal is the worshiper's own and is given on that person's behalf. In 16:21 Aaron leans both hands on the goat's head while confessing Israel's sins over it, and Moses commissions Joshua with the same gesture (Numbers 27:18-23).

decisions.choice: make atonement: put right what stands between the worshiper and God
decisions.reason: The verb is used throughout Leviticus for what the priest does with an offering on someone's behalf. It covers wiping away the stain of sin and impurity (16:30), and paying a ransom for a life (Exodus 30:12-16); the blood given on the altar is the means (17:11). Even the burnt offering, which is not tied to one particular sin, makes atonement: it reconciles the worshiper to God.

decisions.choice: it will be accepted for him: God accepts the offering on the worshiper's behalf
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 7:18 and 22:23-27 of an offering God accepts or refuses.

decisions.choice: lay (Balanced); put (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal says "lean", which is closer to the Hebrew verb. Balanced keeps the familiar "lay his hand on", with "their" for a worshiper who may be a man or a woman; Readable says "put".

decisions.choice: "hacer expiación por" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: "hacer expiación por" keeps the Hebrew verb as one recurring term (m2); Readable keeps it too, as the English Readable keeps "make atonement".

decisions.choice: "faire l'expiation pour" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: "faire l'expiation pour" keeps the Hebrew verb as one recurring term with the worshiper as the one it is done for (m2); Readable keeps it, as the English Readable keeps "make atonement".

decisions.choice: "kufanya upatanisho kwa ajili ya" (L); "kumfanyia upatanisho" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: "upatanisho" (reconciliation) keeps the Hebrew verb as one recurring term and says what it achieves, putting right what stands between the worshiper and God (m2). Balanced and Readable use the applied form "-fanyia" for "for him".

decisions.choice: "chuộc tội cho" for "make atonement for", at every level
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch sheet's wording; the English Readable keeps "make atonement", so Vietnamese does too.

decisions.choice: "속죄하다" for "make atonement" at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet settles "속죄하다"; the English Readable keeps "make atonement" here too. Readable phrases it as "속죄가 이루어진다" to avoid making the animal the grammatical actor.

decisions.choice: "바치는 사람" for "he"
decisions.reason: Korean seldom uses a pronoun for the person in a law; naming him as the one who offers keeps the actor clear where the priest is also active.

decisions.choice: fazer expiação por
decisions.reason: For the whole book (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md): "fazer expiação por" names what the priest does with an offering to put right what stands between the worshiper and God (m2). The English Readable keeps "make atonement", and so does Portuguese Readable; "expiar" alone suggests the worshiper paying for the sin himself.

source.text: וְשָׁחַ֛ט אֶת־בֶּ֥ן הַבָּקָ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְ֠הִקְרִיבוּ בְּנֵ֨י אַהֲרֹ֤ן הַֽכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם וְזָרְק֨וּ אֶת־הַדָּ֤ם עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ סָבִ֔יב אֲשֶׁר־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will slaughter the son of the herd before Yahweh, and will bring near [the] sons of Aaron, the priests, the blood and throw the blood against the altar all around, which [is at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.

en.L: And he shall slaughter the young bull before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall bring near the blood and throw the blood against the altar all around, which [is at] the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.B: The one who brought the young bull is to slaughter it there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Aaron's sons, the priests, are then to present the blood and splash it on every side of the altar that stands at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.R: Then you must kill the young bull there in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Aaron's sons, the priests, will bring the blood. They will splash it on all sides of the altar at the entrance of the meeting tent.

es.L: Y degollará al novillo delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y los hijos de Aarón, los sacerdotes, presentarán la sangre y arrojarán la sangre contra el altar, alrededor, [el altar] que [está a] la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro.
es.B: El que trajo el novillo lo degollará allí, delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Después los hijos de Aarón, los sacerdotes, presentarán la sangre y la salpicarán por todos los lados del altar que está a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro.
es.R: Luego tienes que matar el novillo allí, delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Los hijos de Aarón, los sacerdotes, llevarán la sangre. La salpicarán por todos los lados del altar, a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro.

fr.L: Et il égorgera le jeune taureau devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et les fils d’Aaron, les prêtres, feront approcher le sang et jetteront le sang contre l’autel, tout autour, [l’autel] qui [est à] l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre.
fr.B: Celui qui a amené le jeune taureau l’égorgera là, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Les fils d’Aaron, les prêtres, présenteront ensuite le sang et le projetteront sur tous les côtés de l’autel qui se trouve à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre.
fr.R: Ensuite, tu dois tuer le jeune taureau là, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Les fils d’Aaron, les prêtres, apporteront le sang. Ils le projetteront sur tous les côtés de l’autel, à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre.

sw.L: Naye atamchinja fahali mchanga mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nao wana wa Haruni, makuhani, wataisogeza damu na kuirusha damu kwenye madhabahu pande zote, [madhabahu] iliyo [penye] mlango wa Hema la Kukutania.
sw.B: Yule aliyemleta fahali mchanga atamchinja hapo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kisha wana wa Haruni, makuhani, wataileta damu na kuirusha pande zote za madhabahu iliyo kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania.
sw.R: Kisha lazima umchinje fahali huyo mchanga hapo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wana wa Haruni, makuhani, wataleta damu. Watairusha pande zote za madhabahu, kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 그 수송아지를 잡아야 하고, 아론의 아들들, 곧 제사장들은 그 피를 가까이 가져와서, 회막 입구에 있는 제단 사방에 그 피를 끼얹어야 한다.
ko.B: 수송아지를 가져온 사람은 거기 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 그것을 잡아야 한다. 그러면 아론의 아들들인 제사장들이 그 피를 바치고, 회막 입구에 있는 제단 사방에 그 피를 끼얹어야 한다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 거기 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 수송아지를 잡아야 한다. 아론의 아들들인 제사장들은 그 피를 가져와서, 회막 입구에 있는 제단 둘레에 골고루 끼얹을 것이다.

vi.L: Và người ấy phải giết con bò tơ trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và các con trai A-rôn, là các thầy tế lễ, phải dâng máu và tạt máu lên bàn thờ chung quanh, [là bàn thờ] ở cửa Lều Hội Kiến.
vi.B: Người dâng phải giết con bò tơ ấy tại đó, trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Rồi các con trai A-rôn, là các thầy tế lễ, phải dâng máu và tạt máu lên khắp chung quanh bàn thờ đặt tại cửa Lều Hội Kiến.
vi.R: Rồi người ấy phải giết con bò tơ tại đó, trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Các con trai A-rôn là các thầy tế lễ sẽ đem máu đến. Họ sẽ tạt máu lên khắp bốn phía bàn thờ ở cửa Lều Hội Kiến.

pt.L: E imolará o novilho diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e os filhos de Arão, os sacerdotes, oferecerão o sangue e lançarão o sangue sobre o altar ao redor, que [está à] entrada da tenda do encontro.
pt.B: Quem trouxe o novilho o matará ali, diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Depois os filhos de Arão, os sacerdotes, apresentarão o sangue e o jogarão em todos os lados do altar que fica à entrada da tenda do encontro.
pt.R: Depois deves matar o novilho ali, diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Os filhos de Arão, os sacerdotes, vão trazer o sangue. Eles vão jogá-lo em todos os lados do altar, na entrada da tenda do encontro.

decisions.choice: the son of the herd: a young bull
decisions.reason: "Son of the herd" means a young animal of the cattle, here the male of verse 3.

decisions.choice: the worshiper slaughters; the priests handle the blood
decisions.reason: The one who brings the animal kills it; the priests' work begins with the blood. Only they serve at the altar, the bronze altar of burnt offering that stood in the courtyard before the entrance of the tent (Exodus 27:1-8; 40:6, 29).

decisions.choice: throw the blood against the altar all around: splash it on every side
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw or dash a liquid in quantity, from a bowl; the word for the priests' bowls comes from it (Exodus 27:3). It is different from "sprinkle", done with a finger (4:6). "All around" means that the blood reached every side of the altar.

decisions.choice: splash
decisions.reason: Literal says "throw"; Balanced and Readable say "splash", which describes the action and keeps it distinct from "sprinkle".

decisions.choice: The one who brought the young bull
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he". Balanced names the worshiper so that the reader does not take "he" for the priest, who is first mentioned later in the verse.

decisions.choice: "arrojar" (L); "salpicar" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: the verb means to throw blood in quantity from a bowl (m3). "Rociar" is kept for sprinkling with a finger (4:6), so the two acts stay distinct, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "jeter" (L); "projeter" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: the verb means to throw blood in quantity from a bowl (m3). "Asperger" is kept for sprinkling with a finger (4:6), so the two acts stay distinct, as in the English; "répandre" is kept for pouring out (4:7).

decisions.choice: "kurusha" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Leviticus: the verb means to throw blood in quantity from a bowl (m3). "Kunyunyiza" is kept for sprinkling with a finger (4:6), so the two acts stay distinct, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "tạt máu" for throwing the blood against the altar
decisions.reason: "tạt" is to throw or splash a liquid, which is what the meaning decision describes; "rảy" (sprinkle) is kept for the different verb of sprinkling with the finger (4:6).

decisions.choice: "끼얹다" for throwing or splashing the blood against the altar
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is a throw from a basin, not a sprinkle with the finger; "뿌리다" is kept for the sprinkling of chapters 4-5 so the two acts stay distinct in Korean.

decisions.choice: imolar (L); matar (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Exodus 29:11: Literal says "imolar", the Portuguese verb for slaughtering an animal in sacrifice; Balanced and Readable say "matar", as the English says "slaughter" and "kill". "Abater" sounds like a slaughterhouse.

decisions.choice: lançar (L); jogar (B, R) ... em todos os lados do altar
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the verb means to throw a quantity of liquid from a bowl (m3), so Portuguese uses "lançar" (L) and "jogar" (B, R), keeping "salpicar" for the different verb "sprinkle", done with a finger (4:6), as Exodus 29:21 does and as the English keeps "splash" and "sprinkle" apart. "Aspergir" is left aside because it is used for both in older Bibles.

records.literal_gloss: And he will skin the burnt offering and cut it into its pieces.

en.L: And he shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into its pieces.
en.B: The worshiper is then to skin the burnt offering and cut it up into its parts.
en.R: Then you must take off the animal's skin and cut the animal into its parts.

es.L: Y desollará el holocausto y lo cortará en sus piezas.
es.B: Luego el oferente desollará el holocausto y lo cortará en sus partes.
es.R: Después tienes que quitarle la piel al animal y cortarlo en pedazos.

fr.L: Et il dépouillera l’holocauste et le découpera en ses morceaux.
fr.B: Celui qui l’offre dépouillera ensuite l’holocauste et le découpera en ses différentes parties.
fr.R: Ensuite, tu dois enlever la peau de l’animal et le couper en morceaux.

sw.L: Naye ataichuna ngozi sadaka ya kuteketezwa na kuikata vipande vyake.
sw.B: Kisha anayeitoa ataichuna ngozi sadaka ya kuteketezwa na kuikata vipande vyake.
sw.R: Kisha lazima umchune ngozi mnyama huyo na kumkata vipande vipande.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 번제물의 가죽을 벗기고, 그것을 각 부위로 잘라야 한다.
ko.B: 바치는 사람은 번제물의 가죽을 벗기고 그것을 부위별로 잘라야 한다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 짐승의 가죽을 벗기고 몇 부분으로 잘라야 한다.

vi.L: Và người ấy phải lột da của lễ thiêu và chặt nó thành từng miếng.
vi.B: Rồi người dâng phải lột da con vật dâng làm của lễ thiêu và chặt nó ra thành từng phần.
vi.R: Rồi người ấy phải lột da con vật và chặt nó ra thành từng phần.

pt.L: E esfolará o holocausto e o cortará nos seus pedaços.
pt.B: Depois, quem o oferece tirará a pele do holocausto e o cortará nas suas partes.
pt.R: Depois deves tirar a pele do animal e cortá-lo em partes.

decisions.choice: skin it and cut it into its pieces
decisions.reason: The skin of a burnt offering goes to the priest who offers it (7:8). "Its pieces" are the natural parts of the body, named in verse 8: the head, the fat and the rest.

decisions.choice: he will skin: most likely the worshiper, as in verse 5
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. It is most naturally the one who slaughtered the animal in verse 5. In 2 Chronicles 29:34 it is the priests, helped by the Levites, who skin the burnt offerings.

en.L: And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
en.B: The sons of Aaron the priest are to put fire on the altar and lay wood in order on the fire.
en.R: The sons of Aaron the priest will start a fire on the altar and stack wood on it.

es.L: Y los hijos de Aarón el sacerdote pondrán fuego sobre el altar y dispondrán leña sobre el fuego.
es.B: Los hijos del sacerdote Aarón pondrán fuego en el altar y colocarán leña en orden sobre el fuego.
es.R: Los hijos del sacerdote Aarón encenderán fuego en el altar y apilarán leña encima.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Aaron le prêtre mettront du feu sur l’autel et disposeront du bois sur le feu.
fr.B: Les fils du prêtre Aaron mettront du feu sur l’autel et arrangeront du bois sur le feu.
fr.R: Les fils du prêtre Aaron allumeront un feu sur l’autel et ils empileront du bois dessus.

sw.L: Na wana wa Haruni kuhani wataweka moto juu ya madhabahu na kupanga kuni juu ya moto.
sw.B: Wana wa kuhani Haruni wataweka moto juu ya madhabahu na kupanga kuni kwa utaratibu juu ya moto.
sw.R: Wana wa kuhani Haruni watawasha moto juu ya madhabahu na kupanga kuni juu yake.

ko.L: 그리고 제사장 아론의 아들들은 제단 위에 불을 두고, 그 불 위에 나무를 벌여 놓아야 한다.
ko.B: 제사장 아론의 아들들은 제단에 불을 피우고, 그 불 위에 장작을 가지런히 놓아야 한다.
ko.R: 제사장 아론의 아들들은 제단에 불을 피우고 그 위에 장작을 쌓아야 한다.

vi.L: Và các con trai của thầy tế lễ A-rôn phải đặt lửa trên bàn thờ và xếp củi trên lửa.
vi.B: Các con trai của thầy tế lễ A-rôn phải nhóm lửa trên bàn thờ và xếp củi ngay ngắn trên lửa.
vi.R: Các con trai của thầy tế lễ A-rôn sẽ nhóm lửa trên bàn thờ và chất củi lên.

pt.L: E os filhos de Arão, o sacerdote, porão fogo sobre o altar e arrumarão lenha sobre o fogo.
pt.B: Os filhos do sacerdote Arão porão fogo no altar e arrumarão a lenha em ordem sobre o fogo.
pt.R: Os filhos do sacerdote Arão vão acender um fogo no altar e empilhar lenha em cima dele.

decisions.choice: Aaron the priest: here "priest" is singular
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text "the priest" here is singular and names Aaron, whose sons do the work, whereas verses 5 and 8 say "Aaron's sons, the priests".

decisions.choice: put fire on the altar and arrange wood
decisions.reason: The law assumes a fire on the altar. Later it is commanded that the fire be kept burning and never go out (6:5-6), and when the priests first offered, fire came out from before Yahweh and consumed the offering (9:24).

decisions.choice: start a fire ... stack wood
decisions.reason: Readable says "start a fire" for "put fire" and "stack" for "arrange".

en.B: Aaron's sons, the priests, are to set out the pieces on the burning wood of the altar, along with the head and the suet.
en.R: Then they will place the pieces, the head and the fat on the burning wood on the altar.

fr.B: Les fils d’Aaron, les prêtres, disposeront les morceaux, avec la tête et le suif, sur le bois qui brûle sur l’autel.

sw.L: Na wana wa Haruni, makuhani, watapanga vipande, kichwa na shahamu, juu ya kuni zilizo juu ya moto ulio juu ya madhabahu.
sw.B: Wana wa Haruni, makuhani, watapanga vipande hivyo pamoja na kichwa na shahamu juu ya kuni zinazowaka juu ya madhabahu.
sw.R: Kisha watapanga vipande, kichwa na shahamu juu ya kuni zinazowaka juu ya madhabahu.

ko.L: 그리고 아론의 아들들, 곧 제사장들은 그 조각들과 머리와 굳은 기름을, 제단 위에 있는 불 위에 있는 나무 위에 벌여 놓아야 한다.
ko.B: 아론의 아들들인 제사장들은 그 조각들을 머리와 굳은 기름과 함께 제단의 타는 장작 위에 벌여 놓아야 한다.
ko.R: 그리고 제사장들은 그 조각들과 머리와 기름을 제단 위의 타는 장작 위에 올려놓아야 한다.

vi.L: Và các con trai A-rôn, là các thầy tế lễ, phải xếp các miếng thịt, cái đầu và mỡ trên củi ở trên lửa ở trên bàn thờ.
vi.B: Các con trai A-rôn, là các thầy tế lễ, phải xếp các phần thịt cùng với cái đầu và mỡ lên trên củi đang cháy trên bàn thờ.
vi.R: Rồi họ sẽ đặt các phần thịt, cái đầu và mỡ lên củi đang cháy trên bàn thờ.

pt.L: E os filhos de Arão, os sacerdotes, arrumarão os pedaços, a cabeça e o sebo, sobre a lenha que [está] sobre o fogo que [está] sobre o altar.
pt.B: Os filhos de Arão, os sacerdotes, disporão os pedaços sobre a lenha que arde no altar, junto com a cabeça e o sebo.
pt.R: Depois eles vão colocar os pedaços, a cabeça e a gordura sobre a lenha que está queimando no altar.

decisions.choice: suet: hard fat
decisions.reason: This word for fat occurs only here, in verse 12 and in 8:20. It is probably the hard fat around the inner organs, but it is a different word from "the fat" of chapter 3, and its exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: arrange ... on the wood on the fire on the altar
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the wood in verse 7: things are laid out in order. The chain "wood ... fire ... altar" pictures the offering laid on the fire burning on the altar.

decisions.choice: the fat
decisions.reason: Readable says "the fat" for the rare word Literal and Balanced render "suet".

decisions.choice: "el sebo" (L, B); "la grasa" (R)
decisions.reason: "Sebo" keeps this rare word (m1) apart from "la grasa", used for the common word for the fat in chapter 3, as the English keeps "suet" apart from "fat".

decisions.choice: "le suif" (L, B); "la graisse" (R)
decisions.reason: "Suif" keeps this rare word (m1) apart from "la graisse", used for the common word for the fat in chapter 3, as the English keeps "suet" apart from "fat".

decisions.choice: "shahamu" at every level
decisions.reason: Swahili has no common word for suet apart from fat, so "shahamu" (animal fat) is used here and for the fat of chapter 3; "mafuta" is kept for oil (2:1), so that the two never mix.

decisions.choice: o sebo (L, B); a gordura (R)
decisions.reason: The rare word for hard fat (m1) is "sebo" at Literal and Balanced, so that it stays distinct from "a gordura", the book's word for the fat of chapter 3; Readable says "a gordura", as the English Readable says "the fat".
